instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Comfort Everyone Else
cards.instruction: Meet every painful moment by comforting someone else more intensely while your own distress becomes harder to hide.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I've brought tissues. Being laid off together doesn't make your day any easier.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're wiping your eyes on your sleeve.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. I'm saving the soft ones for you. Tell me what you're worried about.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You. You can't even get the tissue box open.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then take the whole box. I'll make tea once my hands stop doing this.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've decided you're having soup. The choir rejecting us is no reason for you to miss dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: May I set a place for you too?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Approved, for your company. I'll butter your bread first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you sit down now? I don't want you crying alone in the kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may have me beside you. Take my bread as well; I can't swallow yet. But I shall supervise you finishing yours.

cards.title: Emotional Interest
cards.instruction: Treat comfort, vulnerability, and forgiveness as investments that must eventually be repaid with equal emotional risk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I told your mother I'm scared she dislikes me. Sunday, you owe me an equally embarrassing admission.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I didn't ask you to tell her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. I trusted you to risk something too. What scares you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That she'll like you more.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's equal. Now tell her over lunch. Mine had an audience; yours needs one too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I stayed with you all night after you lost your job. I've approved an equally honest conversation about why you've been avoiding me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Does your help come with a bill?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A fair return. You may begin with the reason you stopped answering my calls.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm afraid you'll turn me into another project to manage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That admission is accepted as an installment. Now name one thing I've done that made you feel managed. I invested a whole night; you can risk an example.

cards.title: Ready on My Terms
cards.instruction: Agree to be honest, hopeful, or vulnerable only in forms that preserve your emotional safety.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I'll talk about last night's rent argument, but not the whole year tonight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The whole year matters. You've been pulling away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. It does. One question, and let me finish before you answer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right. Were you going to move out?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I packed a bag. It's still upstairs. Please let that be the whole answer for a minute.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved one conversation about us trying again. I'll take the chair by the door.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Do you need to be able to leave?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Your cooperation with that arrangement is appreciated. You may ask one thing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Would you like to come home? We don't have to decide tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. That answer is authorized to stand alone. You may keep the spare key for now; I'll decide when we're ready to discuss using it.

cards.title: The Same Ending
cards.instruction: Use every new emotional detail as evidence that the same feared ending is becoming inevitable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've decided your 'take care' message begins the breakup. That's how my last one started.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I explain? You said you had a cold.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Explanation permitted. My ex also wanted me healthy before leaving. You may proceed to the next kindness.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I just bring you soup tonight?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Soup is authorized as the farewell meal. Bring a container you don't need back; I won't permit you to prolong the ending with crockery.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've cancelled lunch. I've decided we're at the stage before you stop calling and ask for your key.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: May I be exhausted without ending the relationship?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exhaustion is acknowledged. My ex used that word before seeing me became work.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I book our usual table for tomorrow, then?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Approved for the breakup. He chose a public place too. Request the corner; I will decide how many strangers are permitted to watch me plead.

cards.title: Help Me Keep This Quiet
cards.instruction: Get someone to help contain a secret without first revealing its full risk or purpose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Hide this envelope under the picnic hamper before Mum comes in.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She asked me to unpack the hamper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then keep the envelope in your pocket while you unpack.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll end up taking it home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. I'll explain when she stops asking where it is.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've selected you to hold this cupboard key. Your flatmate is not to hear that I've left it here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I at least know what's in the cupboard?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're cleared to know nothing in it is alive. The rest can wait until tomorrow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then may I insist you collect the key before she comes home?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your deadline is approved. Text me when she leaves work. Just 'key'; you aren't authorized to put your suspicions in writing.
